sentence_stem: What the manager failed to realise
correct_completion: was that the whole team had been working on the wrong project.
full_sentence: What the manager failed to realise was that the whole team had been working on the wrong project.
acceptable_variants: was that the team had spent months on the wrong project.
was that nobody had checked the original brief.

options.text: the whole team had been working on the wrong project.
options.why_wrong: The pseudo-cleft needs a form of 'be' (here 'was') after the 'What' clause to link it to the focus. Without it the sentence is ungrammatical.

options.text: was going to be discussed at the next meeting.
options.why_wrong: This describes a future plan, which does not fit a realisation that the manager missed.

options.text: was that the whole team had been working on the wrong project.
was the lack of experience in the team.
options.why_wrong: Grammatically acceptable, but it names a cause rather than the thing the manager failed to notice, so it does not complete the meaning of the stem.

grammar_focus: Pseudo-cleft sentences with a 'What' clause and a copular verb
explanation: A pseudo-cleft places the focus after a 'What' clause and links the two with a form of 'be'. Learners whose first language builds this structure differently often omit the linking verb, so keep 'was' in English.
translation: O que o gerente não percebeu foi que toda a equipe estava trabalhando no projeto errado.
